method.heading: CMAP Method
method.summary: CMAP arranges executed commands and masked future positions on a shared action tape. HCAT predicts a coarse future chunk and error-supervised uncertainty scores; UGSR selects the contiguous window with the highest mean uncertainty and regenerates only that interval. All surrounding actions are copied unchanged, and only issued commands enter the next execution history.

stages.title: Predict
stages.description: Visual and proprioceptive context combines with the executed-action prefix. The shared coarse features produce continuous future actions and a per-step uncertainty score for every future position.

stages.title: Select
stages.description: UGSR averages uncertainty over every eligible contiguous window and selects the maximum-mean interval R. Actions outside R remain visible as context for refinement.

stages.title: Regenerate
stages.description: The local refiner reconstructs only the masked interval, inserts the refined actions into the preserved tape, and sends the merged chunk to temporal aggregation and closed-loop execution.

simulation.heading: Simulation Experiments
simulation.summary: CMAP is evaluated on six RoboTwin tasks and three single-arm ManiSkill tasks. On RoboTwin, ACT, Diffusion Policy, DDP, and CMAP are evaluated over 100 episodes per task; the comparison also includes published RDT-1B and TwinVLA results.

tables.title: RoboTwin main comparison
tables.note: CMAP is best or tied-best on all six tasks. RDT-1B and TwinVLA values are taken from their original papers.

tables.title: ManiSkill comparison
tables.note: OpenVLA and StaMo are published reference results reported by StaMo; CMAP is best or tied-best on every task.

real_world.heading: Real-World Experiments
real_world.summary: CMAP is compared with ACT, Diffusion Policy, and DDP on four physical tasks across AGIBOT G1 and Leju Kuavo 4 Pro. These deployments test contact-sensitive manipulation, arm-hand coordination, sensing and control delay, and sustained grasp stability.

platforms.title: Long-horizon dexterous manipulation
platforms.description: Kuavo performs Sheet Loading with a 7-DoF arm and dexterous hand from synchronized multi-view RGB observations.

platforms.title: Contact-rich tabletop manipulation
platforms.description: AGIBOT performs three tasks using its right 7-DoF arm and scalar gripper from head- and wrist-camera RGB observations.

table.title: Real-world success counts and rates
table.note: Chess Grasp and Bottle Grasp are measured separately within the same ten Dual-Item Placement trials; the mean weights all five reported success measures equally.

real_world.protocol: All policies use matched task-specific teleoperation data: 50 demonstrations for each AGIBOT task and 150 for Sheet Loading. Each policy is evaluated in ten trials per task, totaling 40 physical rollouts.

ablations.detail: The default configuration uses the full executed history (ρ = 0), one regeneration pass (P = 1), an 8-action interval (L = 8), and temporal aggregation. Guided selection produces mean post-/pre-regeneration error ratios below one on all three held-out tasks, unlike fixed or random intervals.

success_failure.heading: Success, Failure, and Recovery
success_failure.summary: The revised qualitative analysis contrasts successful physical execution with a cup-separation failure and a recovered Sheet Loading near-failure, highlighting two distinct contact challenges.

cases.description: The gripper closes without securing the cup rim, so continued lifting cannot produce a successful separation grasp.
The sheet briefly relies on unstable single-point support; closed-loop replanning recovers while preserving the remaining contact.

success_failure.extension: These cases motivate incorporating contact information into span selection and adapting the regeneration interval to the correction duration required by each task.

title: Predict in Chunks, Revise in Spans: History-conditioned Action Regeneration for Robotic Manipulation
abstract: Action chunking improves temporal coherence in visuomotor imitation learning by jointly predicting sequences of future actions. However, many existing policies regenerate entire action chunks even when errors are localized, potentially replacing otherwise valid predictions. We introduce Contextual Masked Action Policy (CMAP), a visuomotor policy that refines continuous action chunks through history-conditioned local regeneration. Specifically, CMAP introduces a history-conditioned action tape that combines executed commands with masked future positions to produce coarse action predictions and per-step uncertainty scores. An uncertainty-guided span regeneration mechanism then selects a high-uncertainty contiguous span and reconstructs it using the executed history and retained future predictions as context. By jointly reconstructing neighboring actions, CMAP models local temporal dependencies while preserving all predictions outside the selected span. Extensive experiments on nine simulated and four real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate that CMAP achieves superior overall performance over several competitive baselines. Ablation studies validate the complementary contributions of its key components, while held-out trajectory analysis shows that local regeneration reduces prediction errors within selected spans.

hero.alt: Whole-chunk prediction compared with CMAP's history-conditioned local regeneration.
hero.caption: Whole-chunk prediction versus CMAP's editable action tape. Conventional policies regenerate or accept the complete chunk as one object. CMAP uses executed history to localize an unreliable contiguous span, regenerate only that span, and preserve reliable surrounding actions.

method.alt: Overview of the CMAP predict-select-regenerate pipeline.
method.caption: Overview of CMAP. (a) HCAT combines executed history and masked future positions on one action tape, using visual and proprioceptive context to predict coarse actions and error-supervised uncertainty scores. UGSR comprises (b) uncertainty-guided selection of a contiguous span R and (c) regeneration and replacement of that span, with all surrounding actions copied unchanged. Only issued commands update the execution history.
